messages:
alex: thinking out loud — we need a concrete UX + API shape for an automatic fallback policy on rollouts. question: do we surface a single toggle "auto-fallback" or a small DSL for degrade modes?

maria: +1 to thinking about modes. users want predictable behavior: recommend at least two modes: \"soft degrade\" (route small % to fallback while monitoring) and \"hard failover\" (immediate full switch on trigger). :white_check_mark:

tiago: for triggers we should support multiple signals: error-rate, tail-latency (p95/p99), and explicit 5xx/timeout counts. also suggest supporting a combined window: e.g. error_rate > 5% for 120s AND p95 > 1.2s.

jamie: UX note: don't bury the thresholds. show defaults but make them editable per-rollout. default proposal: error_rate 5% sustained 2m, latency p95 1.5s sustained 2m. Default to "recommend" mode (alert + suggested action) unless customer explicitly opts in to "auto-execute".

alex: good. one internal API question: should the rollout object include a \"fallback_chain\" array of model/route IDs or should we accept a single \"fallback\" and handle chaining server-side? pros/cons?

maria: chaining seems useful (multi-tier: cheaper quantized -> last-resort small model). If we require client to pass array it's explicit but more complex. server-side chain lets us provide heuristics, but hides choices from customer. I'd prefer array with optional server-side suggestions.

tiago: +1 for array. also add per-target constraints: max_latency, min_confidence? e.g.:

```json
{
  "policy_type": "auto_fallback",
  "modes": ["soft_degrade"],
  "fallback_chain": ["gpt-q4", "gpt-std-small"],
  "triggers": {
    "error_rate": {"threshold_pct": 5, "window_s": 120},
    "p95_latency_ms": {"threshold": 1500, "window_s": 120}
  },
  "action": "route",
  "dry_run": true
}
```

jamie: love the dry_run flag — UI should surface a \"simulate for X minutes\" that shows what proportion would have been routed and a preview of cost delta and latency impact. allows product to evaluate without flipping the switch.

alex: audit & telemetry: must store the decision event and the state snapshot that led to it for compliance. need to record: rollout_id, policy_id, metric_values_when_triggered, selected_fallback, decision (simulated|executed), user_override if any, and a diff of model versions. how long do we keep this? default 90 days, enterprise option for 1 year.

srebot: auto-note: retention defaults are 90d, enterprise retention configurable. recommend attaching an immutable audit_id and write to audit-store with trace_id for sampling.

maria: UI needs an "audit timeline" on the rollout page showing event markers: trigger check, recommendation generated, action executed, manual revert. clicking marker should show full JSON snapshot + link to logs.

tiago: telemetry: we should emit a couple new metrics: fallback_trigger_count, fallback_success_rate (i.e., did downstream requests succeed after fallback), fallback_cost_delta (estimated tokens cost delta), fallback_latency_change. ensure we tag by org, rollout_id, route. Also surface a small heatmap for per-region variance.

jamie: policy editing UX — if a policy was auto-executed we should prevent blind edits: require a confirmation that mentions last execution time and offers to create a new policy version. also support rollback-to-previous-policy.

alex: open API debate: mandate that auto policies include an "audit_reason" field when enabling auto-execute (free text), or we allow enabling without reason? compliance teams like mandatory explanations. thoughts?

maria: require it for orgs with stricter controls (enterprise only). for self-serve, optional but remind users during onboarding. forcing free text everywhere will annoy devs.

jamie: maybe make it enforced by policy-level flags: \"requires_audit_reason\": true/false. console shows a modal when turning on auto-execute if true.

alex: good approach. last micro-decision: default visibility of auto-fallback decisions — should they be visible to all org members on console or only rollout approvers and auditors?

tiago: default to rollout owners + admins + auditors. let workspace admins configure a broader audience. sensitive info may leak otherwise.

ops-bot: deploybot: rollout-service:staging updated fallback-checker lambda (rev b3c4d) — tests passed.

alex: thanks — can someone sketch a short ticket for eng to implement API + storage + minimal UI? include required telemetry metrics and an acceptance test plan (simulate triggers, verify audit entry and dry_run behavior).

maria: I can draft the ticket and attach the sample policy json above. will ping once ready. :+1:

jamie: I'll mock the modal and audit timeline in Figma and share a link in this thread tomorrow.

alex: awesome — we're converging. leaving this thread open for any edge cases. one more thought: what about quotas? if fallback routes to cheaper model but the quota is consumed differently per model, we need to surface quota impact in the dry-run preview.

tiago: noted — telemetry will compute estimated quota usage per model and surface it.

alex: great, thanks everyone.
